# OpenClaw Tier 1 — Plain-English Overview

This is the plain-English companion to the three Tier 1 specs in `docs/specs/OPENCLAW-IMPORT-*`. Read this first; reach for the spec only if you want every knob and edge case.

## What we're building

Three small imports from OpenClaw, all in Round 1 of the `openclaw-imports` project. Each one is a single PR. Together they tighten how instar handles memory and LLM-call failures.

### 1. Pre-compaction memory flush

**The problem.** When a Claude Code session runs long enough, it compacts its own context to make room. The compaction collapses old turns into a generic summary. Anything the agent learned that wasn't already in `MEMORY.md` can get smoothed out and forgotten.

**The fix.** Run a brief silent turn *just before* compaction. The turn asks the agent: "What from the last hour is durably worth remembering?" Whatever it lists gets written to `MEMORY.md` before the compaction collapses the working memory.

**Why it matters to you.** When your agent suddenly "forgets" something you told it 30 minutes ago, it's almost always because a compaction happened in between. This catches the most important facts before they're lost.

**Knobs.** Off by default until config says otherwise; the model used for the flush can be pinned to a cheap one (Haiku or local Ollama) so it doesn't compete with the main session.

### 2. Cold-start grace knob

**The problem.** The first call to any LLM provider in a fresh process is slower than steady-state — handshakes, auth refresh, the provider's edge server warming up. Today instar silently extends the first call's timeout by 30 seconds. That hidden extension is confusing: operators see a 42-second call and have no idea why a 15-second timeout was honoured as 45 seconds.

**The fix.** Make the grace explicit. New config knob `setupGraceTimeoutMs`. Default zero. Operators who actually want the grace set the value themselves, and every cold-start application gets logged so they can verify it.

**Why it matters to you.** Predictable timeouts and visible cold-start behaviour. No "why is this taking so long" mystery.

**Knobs.** Single global setting in `intelligence.setupGraceTimeoutMs`. Zero means no grace. Anything positive applies on the first call per provider per process.

### 3. Structured fallback-error shape

**The problem.** Instar can chain LLM providers — try Claude-CLI first, fall through to Anthropic API, then to a local Ollama backstop. When every attempt fails today, the caller sees only the *last* attempt's error message. So the agent reports "ECONNREFUSED" when the real story is "tried three providers, two were rate-limited, the third had no network."

**The fix.** A structured error called `FallbackSummaryError` that records every attempt's reason and computes the soonest retry-after across all attempts. The user-facing message becomes "All providers are rate-limited. Soonest retry: in 4 minutes," and the audit log keeps every attempt for engineers to debug from.

**Why it matters to you.** Honest error messages, observable retry timing, debuggable provider failures. When your agent says "all models failed," you'll see *which* and *why* in `.instar/audit/fallback-chain.jsonl`.

**Knobs.** Behind a feature flag `intelligence.fallbackSummaryErrorEnabled` (default on). Flip to off to revert to the old last-attempt-throws-bare behaviour.

## What you're approving

Three small, additive PRs. Each has:

- A spec (the long file you can skip unless you want details).
- A risk assessment section in the spec covering over-block, under-block, latency, spend, rollback.
- Acceptance criteria including CI green on every shard.

All three are zero-spend-on-default for you (subscription path), opt-in by config knobs, and rollback by flipping a flag. No PR touches more than ~6 files; no shared dependencies between the three.

## Order of operations (after your "approve")

1. Build T1.1, T1.2, T1.3 — three separate PRs into instar `main`, parallelisable.
2. Each PR runs through the existing `/instar-dev` gate (pre-commit trace + coveredFiles + artifactSha256), side-effects review, NEXT.md release notes.
3. Pre-push gate verifies version bump + NEXT.md sections.
4. CI green on every shard before merge. `git branch --contains` to verify each commit actually lands on `main`.
5. One consolidated report back when all three are merged — not three separate "PR opened" pings.

## How to approve / push back

- **Approve all three**: reply "approve openclaw tier 1" and I start building.
- **Approve some, defer others**: e.g. "approve T1.2 and T1.3, hold T1.1" — I'll build the approved set and surface a follow-up.
- **Push back on a spec**: tell me what feels wrong and I'll revise that spec before any build.
- **Stop the whole thing**: "halt openclaw imports" — round goes on ice; no work starts.

## What's deferred (won't be in this round)

- Tier 2 (llm-task primitive, before_prompt_build hook) — next round.
- Tier 3 (session pruning, diagnostics state machine) — round after that.
- The 10 deferred-with-reason items in the project plan — re-evaluated only after Tier 3 ships.

- Specs: `docs/specs/OPENCLAW-IMPORT-PRE-COMPACTION-FLUSH-SPEC.md`, `…-COLD-START-GRACE-KNOB-SPEC.md`, `…-FALLBACK-SUMMARY-ERROR-SPEC.md`
